Delete the deployment and redeploy it with Default settings, because a renamed deployment can only be used from the playground

stem: A developer deploys Azure OpenAI gpt-4o-mini in a Foundry project without any extra steps. When the developer deploys a Meta Llama model from the model catalog, Foundry first asks them to accept terms of use, and the same deployment fails for a colleague who lacks some permissions. What explains the difference?

choices.text: Llama models can only be deployed from code, and the portal asks for terms because it is converting the request into an SDK call
Partner models must be fine-tuned before deployment, and accepting the terms starts a training job that needs extra permissions
Llama models run only on provisioned throughput, which needs approval from the subscription owner before Foundry creates the deployment
Models from partners and community need an Azure Marketplace subscription before deployment, while Foundry Models sold by Azure don't

stem: A developer tries to create a second deployment of a model in a Foundry resource. The deployment fails, and the troubleshooting guidance points to a quota exceeded error for that model in the region. Which TWO actions resolve the problem? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Assign a custom guardrail to the new deployment, because the default guardrail counts its scans against the model's quota
Switch the application from API key authentication to Microsoft Entra ID, which raises the quota available to the resource
Submit a quota increase request for that model in the region, so more tokens-per-minute (TPM) can be assigned to deployments
Accept the Azure Marketplace terms for the model again, because quota is only granted with an active Marketplace subscription
Lower the TPM assigned to the existing deployment of that model, which frees quota that the new deployment can use

stem: After an afternoon of testing prompts and settings in the Foundry model playground, a developer wants to start a Python app that sends the same kind of request. What is the quickest way to get a working starting point?

choices.text: Use the Code tab in the playground's chat pane, which shows a sample filled in with the endpoint, deployment name and current settings
Export the chat history as a JSONL file and upload it to the project, where Foundry turns it into a callable function for the app
Use Save as agent, because an app can call a model deployment from Python only after the model has been converted into an agent
Copy the playground's browser URL into the app, because the playground page also acts as a REST endpoint that accepts prompts

stem: A team has deployed three chat models and wants to see which one gives the best answers to its customer questions. Each model must get exactly the same prompt, system message and parameter settings during the test. What should they use?

choices.text: Three browser tabs with one playground each, typing the same prompt into each tab and copying the system message across by hand
Compare mode in the model playground, which runs up to three models side by side with a synchronized prompt and setup
A single deployment that switches between the three models in round-robin order, with the answers logged to Azure Monitor
A fine-tuning job for each model on the same customer questions, then a comparison of the training loss reported for each job

stem: In the Foundry model playground, a developer tunes a gpt-4.1 deployment that drafts replies about a store's warranty terms. Running the same prompt several times gives noticeably different wording, and some replies wander into speculative details. The team wants focused, consistent replies. Which setting change fits best?

choices.text: Raise the maximum output tokens, so every reply has enough room to cover all the warranty terms and leaves less space for invented details
Change the deployment type to Global Standard, because that deployment type returns the same reply every time the same prompt is sent
Lower the temperature, for example to about 0.2, so the model favors its most likely word choices and the replies stay focused and consistent
Raise the temperature toward its maximum of 2, so the model weighs many more candidate words and then settles on the most accurate wording

stem: A chat client calls a model deployment through Chat Completions. For one user's message, the call fails with HTTP status 400 and an error code of content_filter. Other users' messages work normally. What happened?

choices.text: The deployment's guardrail classified the user's prompt as harmful at a blocked severity level, so the request was rejected
The model started a reply but was cut off at the maximum output token limit, so the service returned the partial text as an error
The conversation history grew larger than the model's context window, so the service rejected the request before generating a reply
The app exceeded the deployment's tokens-per-minute allocation, so the service throttled this request and asked it to retry

stem: A developer writes a Python script with the Foundry SDK. They have the project endpoint and a deployment named gpt-4.1. Which sequence sends a prompt to the model and prints the reply?

choices.text: Create a DefaultAzureCredential() and call its get_token() method with the prompt text as the scope, then print the text inside the returned token
Create an AIProjectClient with the endpoint and the deployment name gpt-4.1, call project.deployments.run(prompt), then print the returned content_text property
Create an AIProjectClient with only DefaultAzureCredential(), call get_openai_client(endpoint=endpoint), then call responses.create(input=prompt) with no model name
Create an AIProjectClient with the endpoint and DefaultAzureCredential(), call get_openai_client(), call responses.create(model="gpt-4.1", input=prompt), then print output_text

stem: A developer is starting a new Python chat app that uses the OpenAI-compatible client from get_openai_client(). It calls a gpt-4.1 deployment now and might later switch to a Foundry direct model such as Microsoft Phi. The developer wants the chat API that Microsoft recommends for new projects. Which choice fits, and why?

choices.text: The Responses API, but only after the deployment is saved as an agent, because responses.create can only send prompts to agents and not to models
The Responses API, because it's recommended for most new development, supports stateful multi-turn chats, and also works with Foundry direct models
The ChatCompletions API, because the Responses API has no way to set a system prompt, so the rules would have to be repeated in every user input
The ChatCompletions API, because it is the only one of the two chat APIs that works with Foundry direct models as well as with Azure OpenAI models

stem: A console chat app keeps a list that starts with a system message. In a loop it appends the user's input, calls chat.completions.create(model=..., messages=conversation) and prints the reply. When a user asks "Who founded it?" after a question about Microsoft, the model doesn't know what "it" means. What is missing?

choices.text: The app must start a new client object for each question, because a reused client mixes up the order of the earlier messages
The app must set the store parameter to true, so the service keeps the conversation and attaches the earlier turns on the next call
The app must move the user's first question into the system message, because the model only remembers what the system role says
The app must append each reply to the list as an assistant message, so the next call sends the full conversation back to the model

stem: A console chat client calls responses.create and prints response.output_text once the call returns. For long answers, users say the app seems to freeze for many seconds before any text appears. The answers themselves are fine. What change improves the experience most directly?

choices.text: Pass stream=True and print each text delta as it arrives, so the user sees the reply build up while the rest is still being generated
Switch to the AsyncOpenAI client and await the same single call inside asyncio.run(), so each individual reply comes back much sooner
Lower max_output_tokens to a small value, so every reply finishes sooner even if long answers are cut off before the model completes them
Create a new deployment of the same model for every user, so each user's requests run on a dedicated copy and get answers instantly

stem: A developer sends this list to chat.completions.create: a system message describing a tax helper; a user message "When do I need to file?"; an assistant message with a link to the filing page; and a user message "How do I check my refund?". Which TWO statements about this request are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The system message must move to the end of the list, because the model only applies the instructions it reads last
The list ends with a user message, which signals that it's the assistant's turn to respond to the refund question
The model will store this list after the call, so the next request can send just the next question without earlier turns
The assistant message is ignored, because only the model can produce messages with the assistant role in a conversation
The earlier user and assistant pair acts as a few-shot example of the kind of answer the developer wants from the model

stem: A developer's first prototype creates an OpenAI client with the Azure OpenAI endpoint and the resource's API key pasted into the source code. Before sharing the app with other teams, they review authentication. Which assessment matches Microsoft's guidance?

choices.text: Keys are the recommended choice for production because they never expire, while Microsoft Entra ID tokens stop working after an hour and break running apps
Keys are acceptable only if the app also calls the project endpoint with AIProjectClient, which adds role checks on top of the key automatically
Keys grant full access with no role restrictions, so prefer Microsoft Entra ID; if a key is still needed, store it in Azure Key Vault, not in code
Keys and Microsoft Entra ID give identical security, because both are checked against the same Azure RBAC role assignments on the resource

stem: A console chat client uses Chat Completions and sends the full conversation on every turn. After a long session, requests start failing even though short conversations still work. Nothing in the deployment has changed. What is the likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The client object expires after a set number of calls; create a new OpenAI client and resend the full conversation history to the model
The temperature drifts upward during long sessions and makes the model fail; set temperature to zero again before each request
The history plus the requested output exceeds the model's token limit; track the token count and send only recent turns that fit
The deployment's guardrail blocks long conversations as a possible prompt attack; assign a guardrail that turns off user prompt attack detection
